scope.unitOfComposition: ordered glyph instances in a word or authored composition

authority.note: The solver proposes and validates relationships; it does not rewrite glyph masters or mutate Three.js meshes.

principles: A connection is optional; deliberate open separation is a valid relationship.
Anchor compatibility creates candidates, not accepted connections.
Relationship type is stored separately from its geometric realization.
All accepted relationships are stable-ID graph records and reversible.
Glyph identity, protected negative spaces and declared topology outrank visual density.
No opaque single graffiti score; expose separate measurements and reasons.
Pair decisions must be rechecked in whole-word context.
Three.js interaction submits typed commands against canonical composition state.

relationshipTypes.geometry: no joining geometry; preserve deliberate inter-letter gap
contours approach within a declared proximity band but remain disjoint
compatible terminals meet or align with declared continuity
two authored bars align as a visual continuation; distinct source components remain addressable
glyph contours overlap with explicit occlusion/layer order; no semantic merge implied
separate authored extension links two declared roots; never counted as a glyph stroke
two glyph constructions reference a shared semantic/vector component; topology and identity review required
multiple parts weave with explicit crossing order and validated negative-space channels

rules: Stable anchor IDs must survive geometry regeneration unless the authored variant changes the anchor identity.
Direction must be nonzero and normalized for comparison; authored and derived directions retain provenance.
An anchor is a bounded usable zone with clearance, not a naked point.
Allowed connection types and compatibility tags are explicit; no wildcard compatibility by default.
Anchors on provisional glyphs are advisory and cannot authorize production-grade joins.

process: construct reversible candidate transform or relationship geometry
candidateGeneration.noHardcodedPairMatrix: Do not use a 26x26 pair table as the sole compatibility source. Optional curated preferences may bias ranking but cannot bypass geometric checks.
candidateGeneration.deterministic: Stable candidate IDs derive from stable instance/anchor/type IDs and solver version, not array order or random values.

pairMetrics.meaning: distance between intended anchor contact/continuation positions
angular relation between anchor directions and relationship tangent
minimum distance to protected geometry around both anchors
unintended intersections or collisions introduced by the candidate
declared front/back order and visible component continuity
measured local mass and gap behavior; review metric, not an identity override
relative cap-height, width and mass balance

hardGates: anchor IDs and glyph references resolve
relationship type allowed by both anchors
glyph transforms remain within declared constraints
no unintended contour collision or self-intersection
protected counters and apertures remain valid
required channel clearance passes calibrated profile
evaluationPolicy.ranking: Use a transparent weighted vector or lexicographic preference profile declared by composition grammar. Always show component metrics; never hide trade-offs behind one uninspectable score.
evaluationPolicy.rejection: Any hard-gate failure rejects the candidate; a high soft score cannot override it.
evaluationPolicy.experimental: Experimental grammar combinations may be previewed with warnings but cannot be silently promoted to supported.

graphConstraints: No duplicate active relationship for same anchor pair unless explicitly multi-edge capable
No cycles that imply contradictory layer order
Shared-stroke edges require shared component references
Extension bridges remain separate semantic components
Open separation may be stored as an explicit user choice or inferred layout state but is not a geometric join

phases: select pair relations under local hard constraints
check non-adjacent collisions and occlusion cycles
recompute channels and protected negative spaces across entire word
evaluate word silhouette, rhythm and legibility metrics
persist reversible accepted graph and user overrides
globalChecks: counter/aperture occlusion by any glyph or extension
wordSolver.localEditPolicy: When one glyph changes, invalidate relationships incident to that glyph plus global checks affected by its changed bounds/geometry; preserve unrelated accepted edges when still valid and report invalidated edges.

userInteraction.selection: Select a relationship edge or anchor by stable ID in Three.js viewport.
userInteraction.preview: Drag creates an ephemeral candidate preview; it does not mutate canonical state.
userInteraction.commit: Release emits one typed relationship command with expected composition revision.
userInteraction.override: Manual accepted/rejected candidate decisions are stored as explicit overrides with rationale and are revalidated after dependent edits.
userInteraction.undoRedo: Undo/redo replays canonical graph patches through the same validator.
userInteraction.diagnostics: Show why candidate passed/failed, affected anchors/components and measured metrics.
forbidden: direct mesh mutation as persisted relationship
decorative bridge counted as structural join
automatic glyph-master mutation to force a join

diagnostics.meaning: Relationship references an unknown anchor or glyph instance.
Relationship type is not permitted by both anchors.
Anchor directions do not meet the selected relationship preference.
Candidate exceeds calibrated anchor position envelope.
Candidate collapses a protected negative-space channel.
Candidate introduces an undeclared contour collision.
Crossing/interlock has no explicit valid layer order.
Relationship graph contains contradictory layer ordering.
Relationship requires an invalid glyph identity change.
Pair is valid but reduces preferred whole-word flow.
A stored user override requires revalidation after a dependency changed.
Relationship relies on a provisional glyph/anchor and is not production-certified.

rollout.name: Advanced structural weaving
requirements: human visual review and experimental grammar gate

testFixtures.purpose: intentional gap persists as explicit relationship
near-touch does not create false contour merge
incompatible directions are rejected or warned per hard/soft policy
candidate that obscures protected counter fails
candidate that closes G aperture fails
bar continuation preserves source component identities
editing one glyph invalidates dependent edges, preserves unaffected edges
same inputs and solver version reproduce candidates and diagnostics
relationship graph restores exactly after undo/redo

acceptanceCriteria: Pair candidates derive from anchors and context rather than a hardcoded pair table.
Open separation is represented as a valid intentional choice.
Relationship type is separate from its geometric realization.
Every accepted edge has stable IDs and a validation report.
No decorative bridge is counted as a true glyph join.
Hard topology and identity constraints override soft composition preferences.
Pair decisions are rechecked in whole-word context.
Three.js editing commits through typed commands and canonical graph patches.
Manual overrides survive save/load and are revalidated after dependencies change.
Phase 1 works before shared strokes and interlocking are attempted.
